title: The Big Laddoo
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Imagine the big picture
levels.teaching_goal: Notice how a poem uses an impossible big image to make the reader imagine and smile.

guided_check.teaching_block: In this poem, the fun comes from imagining ordinary things becoming huge. A laddoo is small in real life, but the poem asks us to picture one giant laddoo.
guided_check.passage: Imagine every sweet laddoo in the town joining into one huge round sweet.
guided_check.prompt: What giant sweet is the poem asking us to imagine?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: find the food word first. The poem stretches that food into a very large picture.
bridge.passage: The child looks at the giant sweet and laughs at its size.
bridge.prompt: Which food is being imagined as giant?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: poems can exaggerate. Exaggerate means to make something much bigger or stronger than real life.
masterclass.passage: The child imagines one huge laddoo rolling near a wide sea.
masterclass.prompt: Which word tells the poem is using an exaggerated image?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now infer the sound picture without hints.
independent_check.passage: A giant sweet falls into a wide sea and water jumps everywhere.
independent_check.prompt: What kind of sound or action would this make?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Recognise playful exaggeration in a new setting. Decide what ordinary object has been made impossibly large and what effect that creates.
transfer_check.passage: In Jatin's funny tale, one school eraser is as large as a bus. It rubs out an entire chalk road in one sweep.

levels.title: Sort round things
levels.teaching_goal: Classify round things by whether they are food or not food.

guided_check.teaching_block: Many things can be round. The important question is not only shape, but also category: can we eat it?
guided_check.passage: A laddoo, a coin, a ball, and an orange are all round.
guided_check.prompt: Which round thing is a sweet food?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: first check the shape, then check if it is food. A laddoo is round and edible.
bridge.passage: The child keeps a round sweet on a plate.
bridge.prompt: Which word names the round sweet?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: classification uses two clues. Shape clue: round. Food clue: can be eaten.
masterclass.passage: A round orange can be eaten. A round ball cannot be eaten.
masterclass.prompt: Which item is round but cannot be eaten?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose a round thing that is not food.
independent_check.passage: Round things: laddoo, ball, orange, chapatti.
independent_check.prompt: Which round thing should go in the cannot-be-eaten column?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer two-clue classification to a classroom sorting task. Check both shape and use before deciding.
transfer_check.passage: Objects: a round biscuit, a rubber ball, a button, and a guava. The teacher asks for a round object used to fasten a shirt.
transfer_check.prompt: Which object belongs in that group?

levels.title: Use sense clues
levels.teaching_goal: Use touch, smell, and taste clues to identify food when a picture clue is missing.

guided_check.teaching_block: Sometimes a person knows an object without seeing it. They may use touch, smell, or taste clues.
guided_check.passage: Meena cannot see the sweet clearly. She feels its round shape in her hand.
guided_check.prompt: Which sense helps Meena feel the shape?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: touch tells shape and texture. Smell tells aroma. Taste tells flavour.
bridge.passage: The sweet is round in Meena's hand and smells like cardamom.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: a strong answer names the clue and the conclusion. She knew it was a laddoo because it felt round and smelled sweet.
masterclass.passage: A child feels a round sweet and notices a sweet smell.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer uses the clues best?

independent_check.teaching_block: Combine different senses instead of repeating one clue. State the food and the evidence that supports the guess.
independent_check.passage: Without looking, Ritu touches a cool, smooth slice and smells fresh cucumber.
independent_check.prompt: What food does Ritu identify, and which clues help her?

concept_slots.description: Identifies cucumber.
Uses a touch clue.
Uses the cucumber smell clue.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use sensory evidence outside the sweets theme. A strong explanation names the object and at least two clues.
transfer_check.passage: With his eyes closed, Veer hears a crisp crunch and tastes salty masala on a thin slice.
transfer_check.prompt: What snack might Veer be eating, and what evidence supports the guess?

concept_slots.description: Identifies a chip or crisp.
Uses the crunch sound.
Uses the salty or masala taste.

levels.title: Write a sensory picture
levels.focus: use adjectives in a complete sentence
levels.teaching_goal: Choose precise describing words and combine them with a noun and action to create a clear food image.

guided_check.teaching_block: A describing word tells what kind, which one, or how something feels. In 'warm golden laddoo', warm and golden describe the laddoo.
guided_check.passage: The warm golden laddoo rests on a silver plate.

bridge.teaching_block: First name the food, then choose a detail that belongs to it. An action word such as melts tells what the food does, not what kind it is.
bridge.passage: The soft sweet peda melts in my mouth.

masterclass.teaching_block: Do not mistake any nearby word for a describing word. A complete sensory sentence needs a food noun, a fitting detail, and an action or linking verb.
masterclass.passage: Food: jalebi. Detail: crisp. Action: glows in the shop window.
masterclass.prompt: Which sentence uses all three parts clearly?
options: The crisp jalebi glows in the shop window.
accepted_answers: the crisp jalebi glows in the shop window
the crisp jalebi glows in the shop window.

independent_check.teaching_block: Create a new sensory sentence from notes. Use the details naturally rather than copying the note order.
independent_check.passage: Food note: kheer | creamy | smells of cardamom | served in a blue bowl.
independent_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence that helps a reader imagine the kheer.

concept_slots.description: Names kheer.
Uses creamy or the cardamom smell.
Mentions the blue bowl.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Transfer descriptive sentence writing to a non-food object while keeping noun, detail, and action clear.
transfer_check.passage: Object note: rain cloud | dark, heavy | moves over the playground.
transfer_check.prompt: Write one complete sentence describing the cloud.

concept_slots.description: Names the rain cloud.
Uses dark or heavy as a describing word.
States that it moves over the playground.

levels.title: Float or sink
levels.teaching_goal: Use light and heavy clues to predict whether an object may float or sink in water.

guided_check.teaching_block: When an object stays on top of water, it floats. When it goes down into water, it sinks.
guided_check.passage: A dry leaf stays on top of the water.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: light objects often float. Heavy objects often sink.
bridge.passage: A feather stays on top of the water.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: compare two objects. A leaf may float; a small stone usually sinks.
masterclass.passage: A small stone drops to the bottom of a tub.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the word without hints.
independent_check.passage: A stone goes down to the bottom of the water.
independent_check.prompt: Write the action word: float or sink.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply float-and-sink vocabulary to a classroom test with a different material. Use what happens in the water as the deciding clue.
transfer_check.passage: A lump of modelling clay drops to the bottom of a bucket, but the same clay floats after Mina shapes it like a hollow bowl.
transfer_check.prompt: What does the hollow clay bowl do?

items.passage: A cook dreams that one laddoo grows wider than the market square. Children use ladders to sprinkle nuts on its top.
accepted_answers: the cook imagines a huge laddoo

items.passage: In a playful verse, a pancake becomes a flying carpet and carries breakfast over the rooftops.

concept_slots.description: Explains that a pancake cannot really fly or become a carpet.

items.passage: A mountain-sized sweet rolls down the road, so everyone steps aside.
options: the huge sweet may hit them
they want it to stop being round
accepted_answers: the huge sweet may hit them

items.passage: Objects: coin, puri, marble, wheel. Choose the round object that is eaten with a meal.
Objects: orange, rubber ring, chapatti, bangle. One is round, worn on the wrist, and not food.
The bread is crisp outside but soft inside.
items.prompt: Which two words describe the bread?

items.passage: The fragrant soup bubbles in the steel pot.
Food note: hot corn | buttery smell | served in a paper cup.

concept_slots.description: Names corn.
Uses hot or buttery as a detail.
Mentions the paper cup.

items.passage: Food note: ripe mango | juicy, golden | lies beside the knife.
items.prompt: Write one complete sentence that creates a clear picture.

concept_slots.description: Names the mango.
Uses juicy or golden.
Gives its place beside the knife.

items.passage: Asha cannot see the bowl. She smells lemon and feels cold, slippery noodles with a spoon.
items.prompt: Which two senses give her clues?

items.passage: A closed lunchbox gives off a smoky paneer smell. When opened, it feels warm.
items.prompt: Explain what two clues suggest about the food.

concept_slots.description: Infers that the food is warm, cooked, or freshly prepared.
Uses both the smoky smell and warm touch.

items.passage: Ravi hears a crackle and smells roasted peanuts before the packet is opened.
items.prompt: Why might he guess the snack is crunchy?

concept_slots.description: Uses the crackle as evidence.
Connects the sound to a crunchy snack or peanuts.

items.passage: A dry cork stays on the water's surface.
An iron key drops to the bottom of a jug.
A foil sheet sinks when crumpled tightly but floats when shaped like a wide tray.
The cook divides one huge sweet among every child instead of giving it to one winner.
items.prompt: Why is dividing it a fair choice?

concept_slots.description: Mentions sharing or dividing the sweet.
Explains that every child receives a part.

items.passage: The giant laddoo cracks open, and hundreds of tiny sweets roll toward the waiting crowd.
items.prompt: What happens after the laddoo cracks?
accepted_answers: tiny sweets roll toward the crowd

items.passage: A poet says a pea grows into a green moon above the dinner table.
Object note: soap bubble | clear, delicate | drifts above the sink.

concept_slots.description: Names the soap bubble.
Uses clear or delicate.
Says that it drifts above the sink.

items.passage: A child predicts that a hollow orange peel will sink. It stays on top during the test.
items.prompt: State what the test shows and why the prediction must change.

concept_slots.description: States that the peel floats or stays on top.
Explains that the observed result disproves the sinking prediction.
